summary: In Greek mythology, Actaea or Actea (Ancient Greek Ἀκταία, "dweller on coasts") is the Nereid of the rocky shore, one of the fifty sea-nymph daughters of Nereus and the Oceanid Doris. Homer names her among the sisters who gather around Thetis in grief for Achilles after Patroclus' death; Hesiod and Apollodorus include her in the Nereid catalogues.
etymology: From ἀκτή, "seashore" — the Nereid associated with rocky coasts.

sections.heading: Nereid of the shore
paragraphs: Actaea belongs to the Hesiodic and Homeric catalogues of Nereus' daughters. In Iliad 18 she and her sisters appear when Thetis cries out in sympathy for Achilles' grief over Patroclus — a catalogue appearance rather than an independent adventure cycle.
The name Actaea was also borne by a Danaid (daughter of Danaus and Pieria) and by the former name of Attica under King Actaeus; those are distinct figures.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id actaea is the Nereid alone. The Danaid Actaea is actaea-danaid; Attic Actaeus/Actaea as a place-name tradition is not this node.
